c-di-GMP regulates bacterial antioxidant defense through the transcriptional regulator, HpoR.

the second messenger molecule c-di-GMP is involved in regulation of mycobacterial HPOX gene cluster and that HpoR, a c-di-GMP responsive transcriptional regulator, acts as an inhibitor for the gene cluster.
HpoR is a novel c-diGMP effective regulator in M. smematis and that H2O2 induces c-di-GM accumulation in M. sengmatis.

the c-di-Gmp signal and its regulatory function on the mycobacterial redox homeostasis.
the c-di-GMO signal in mycobacteria and provides a novel insight into the regulation mechanism of bacterial antioxidant defense.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
c-di-GMP regulates the hpoR expression in M. smematis via HpoR.
c-di-GMP regulates the hpoR gene expression in mycobacteria by directly binding to HpoR.
the c-di-Gmp signal participates in regulation the mycobacterial redox homeostasis through HpoR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
c-di-GMP acts as a positive regulator of the mycobacterial oxidative response and H2O2 tolerance.
c-di-GMP is a novel signal molecule that regulates bacterial antioxidant response through a c-di-GMP effector, HpoR.
the c-di-Gmp signaling regulates the mycobacterial redox homeostasis by controlling the expression of a hpoR operonic gene cluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that

H2O2 induces c-di-GM accumulation, which triggers expression of hpoR operons, and high level of cdi-GMP de-represents the association of HpoRs with the hpoR promoters, thus conferring the mycobacterial resistance against H2O2.
the c-di-G-MP signal is involved in regulation of bacterial oxidative stress response and that the c-di-g-MP signal is linked to the antioxidant regulation in mycobacteria through HpoR.
c-di-GMP is a global signaling factor that modulates a broad range of cellular processes, including bacterial antioxidant defense.
